source: #157 stage 4, Claude Code same-id resume on the herdr rail, under main 68bd94's GO (07697d) relaying GLG's direct approval, with the facts from lead 915040's bundle (the herdr-resume-call and v2 visible-resume source and the S4-CC-A H1/H2 receipt): inside herdr every resumable backend opens in a new herdr tab, Claude Code through ONE layout.apply observed by joining its receiver marker to the pane's direct child, and pane-process-unread when herdr reports none. Provenance, not blended with any earlier layer's: Opus 169dd1 copied the old values from the 2734f524 Root text before any producer edit and wrote the new literals in the same pass; they were NOT approved before it, and their independent review is 915040's cross-review and the Fable joint review requested for this bundle, which this file does not record. The MCP resume description stays inside the 2048-character host cap.

amendments.old: Only on an explicit operator request, reopen ONE DORMANT pi, pi-durable or Claude Code citizen under its OWN garden id, in a visible window in the operator's own tmux session — or, for pi or pi-durable inside herdr, a new herdr tab. The record supplies session, cwd and, for pi, the transcript's model and provider; the only input is the target id (no model override, task or prompt). Claude Code returns as `claude --resume <session id>` without its earlier model or permission flags. This verb submits NO prompt; what the runtime does once back (for Claude Code, unread mail may wake a turn) is not measured; talking to it is still entwurf_v2 fire-and-forget. TWO receipts mean different things: a LAUNCH receipt (a tmux window or herdr tab was made and asked to start the runtime) and an OBSERVATION receipt (pi: the control socket answered under the same id; pi-durable: the started child adopted this call's reservation (not readiness), or not-yet-adopted / reservation-lost; Claude Code: a NEW live process in this call's window re-armed the session's marker with a fresh binding in the record; or resume-unobserved, or record-unreadable with its cause). Unobserved is an outcome, not an error to retry; read the visible window. A session a live process holds is refused: a running citizen is reached only via entwurf_v2's rail check; an unadopted pi-durable reservation is not reachable by entwurf_v2. pi-durable reopens only if its session claim is closed and released or its holder is proven gone. Claude Code reopens only if the last validated owner its Entwurf hook armed is proven gone AND that arm is still the record's last; a missing, unreadable, mismatched or unbound marker or an inconclusive owner refuses, and a session held without a committed hook attach is invisible to that proof. Other backends have no same-id resume. This agent itself must run inside tmux, or inside herdr for a pi or pi-durable target (Claude Code is refused there, never sent to tmux).

amendments.old: Only on an explicit operator request, reopen ONE dormant pi, pi-durable or Claude Code citizen under its own garden id in a visible tmux window — or, for pi or pi-durable inside herdr, a new herdr tab — through the entwurf-bridge (target required; the record supplies the session and cwd — no task or prompt is submitted). Returns the bridge's LAUNCH and OBSERVATION receipts or its named refusal: a session a live process holds (a running citizen, or a pi-durable reservation awaiting adoption), another backend, or a citizen not proven dormant is refused by name, and opening it needs the tmux session — or, for pi or pi-durable only, the herdr pane — this host itself was launched in; a Claude Code target inside herdr is refused, never sent to tmux. Existing unread mail may still wake the resumed runtime; neither receipt proves what it did.

Returns the bridge's LAUNCH and OBSERVATION receipts or its named refusal: a session a live process holds (a running citizen, or a pi-durable reservation awaiting adoption), another backend, or a citizen not proven dormant is refused by name, and opening it needs the tmux session — or the herdr pane — this host itself was launched in; a herdr launch never falls back to tmux. Existing unread mail may still wake the resumed runtime; neither receipt proves what it did.
